messages:
jess: Heads-up — noticed a fragmentation spike in apse1 this morning. Reserved jobs losing locality, lots of tiny pods filling warm nodes and leaving holes on reserved racks.
omar: Yep, metrics show packing fragmentation jumped from 0.12 -> 0.38 around 03:14 UTC. Preemptions for batch jobs up 45% in last hour.
infra-bot: ALERT: apse1.fragmentation.p90=0.38, preemptions=67/1h, warmpool.fill_rate=low. link: https://metrics.redwood/apse1/packing
liam: Root cause looks like a combination: (1) recent label change for gpu.type (a100->a100x) causing strict affinity rejects, (2) autoscaler warm-pool added many small nodes without proper taint for spot jobs, (3) scheduler reschedules aggressively causing attach churn & evictions.
sasha: Sample scheduler filter log: ```E10:03 scheduler: pod/train-99 filtered node/node-87: missing label gpu.type=a100x (node has gpu.type=a100)```
amira: We also saw kubelet attach latency spike in the same timeframe. When scheduler bounces pods, attach-controller queue gets a burst and timeouts happen, so the churn cascades.
jess: Immediate mitigations: 1) add alias mapping in scheduler predicates to accept gpu.type in {a100, a100x}; 2) pause warm-pool scale-ups for 30m; 3) apply a 10m placement_grace to avoid aggressive rebinds; 4) throttle attach-controller concurrent attaches in apse1.
omar: I can push the alias map as a hot config change and hot-reload scheduler. That should reduce new rejects quickly.
liam: I'll open a small PR to backfill taints on warm nodes so spot workloads get the "spot=true" taint, preventing them from filling reserved capacity.
sasha: Also recommend a quick defrag run after alias fix: drain the smallest warm nodes, let scheduler binpack onto matching nodes, then scale warm-pool back to target. Schedule during low traffic window 02:00-04:00 UTC.
infra-bot: ACTION: created INFRA-7219 "gpu.type-label-alias + defrag"; assigned to eng-platform.
nora: Post-incident actions: add metric gpu.label_mismatch_rate, surface attach_controller.queue_depth per-AZ, and add a runbook section "label-alias causing fragmentation". Also add an opt-in conservative reschedule flag for reserved pools.
amira: Quick note on cost: fragmentation is estimated to be wasting ~12% of reserved GPU capacity in apse1 (monthly ~$28k). We should include cost impact in the incident ticket.
jess: Agreed — will add cost calc. For now, performing alias hotfix canary in apse1a. If canary looks good, roll to rest of apse1 then us-west2.
omar: Canary result: rejects dropped to <1% in 6m, fragmentation moved from 0.38 -> 0.17. Rolling out now.
liam: After rollout, starting defrag job in phased manner: drain 6 warm nodes at a time, wait for binpack stable, monitor attach queue.
sasha: Reminder: while draining, watch for attach_controller queue, don't exceed 60 concurrent attaches. If queue grows, pause drains.
infra-bot: NOTE: attach-controller.queue_depth after rollout=28, median_attach_latency=22s.
nora: Closing actions: add alias mapping tests to CI, run a weekly label-consistency check, and add an SLO for attach-controller retry storms.
jess: Thanks all — filing the postmortem and scheduling the defrag tonight. :white_check_mark:
